findings.evidence: Configuration or migrations go first when later behavior needs them, not last by category. Independent groups: contracts first, tests and docs last.
findings.fix: Remove the generic ordering rule 'contracts first, tests and docs last', which the model already applies. Keep only the non-obvious override that configuration and migrations go first when later behaviour depends on them.

findings.evidence: Group files by purpose (not by directory), one group per reviewable idea. ... merge groups that cannot be understood apart.
findings.fix: Add 2-3 decision questions for unclear dependency direction, for example: 'When a refactor and a feature change the same call site, ask which one a reviewer needs first to read the other; a test changed with its implementation joins that group unless it tests a contract other groups also use.'

findings.evidence: State only what the patch proves. Mark author intent that you infer as inferred; the diff does not show why.
findings.fix: Make this a concrete gotcha. For example: 'A deleted function plus a new function with a similar body is not proof of a rename (check callers); a moved file shown as delete+add without -M is still a move; say so instead of describing it as new code.'

findings.evidence: reply "Please paste or describe the changes you want me to analyze in your next message." and wait.
findings.fix: Add the follow-up branch: if the user describes changes instead of pasting a patch, say the report rests on the description, skip the size check and the manifest check (there are no `diff --git` headers), and mark every group as described rather than proved by a patch. If the pasted text has no `diff --git` headers, ask once for a unified diff.
